key_insight: For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, neural approximation power alone is insufficient: convergence also requires stable trial classes, adequate collocation sampling, and accurate admissible comparison networks.
engineering_relevance: The framework guides PINN design by linking trial-class constraints, collocation-point requirements, and scale-dependent boundary weighting to solution-error control.
method: Use elliptic regularity to bound solution error by continuous PDE and boundary residuals.
Identify admissible neural subclasses whose discrete residual loss controls continuous residuals with physics-balanced boundary weighting.
Construct admissible tanh-MLP comparison networks to prove constrained convergence and conditional unconstrained convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence results for tanh-MLPs, not numerical benchmarks or empirical performance measurements.
watch_item: Unconstrained PINN convergence is conditional and requires joint network and sampling refinement; approximation guarantees alone do not suffice.
paper_title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
